record.what_it_does: FX audit API scoring bank/card FX rates against live mid-market rates, with MCP server.
record.auth_notes: Bearer API keys (ipx_live_ / ipx_test_) generated in the dashboard. No OAuth, so each end user would need to supply their own key.
record.access_notes: The free tier gives 3 lifetime audits. The homepage says API access needs the Credit Pack ($99 for 100 audits) or Unlimited ($299/mo). The MCP free tools are limited to 10 audits/day and 60 rate calls/min per key. The pricing page lists no separate API plans, so the exact gating is unclear.
record.api_breadth_notes: 3 endpoints: POST /audit, GET /rates, POST /audit/document. The MCP server has 3 tools.
record.mcp_notes: https://hvujzsdwcoweirroubeh.supabase.co/functions/v1/mcp-server (SSE, Bearer auth). It is linked from ipayx.ai/docs/mcp-server.
record.blocker_notes: The API has only 3 endpoints, and the product is niche. Full API access appears to need a paid plan. Auth is a per-user API key. Sandbox ipx_test_ keys are mentioned only on the MCP docs page.

evidence.quote: REST API + SDKs for FX audit automation.
Upgrade to the 100-audit Credit Pack or Unlimited for API access, white-label embedding, and forensic PDF exports.
POST /audit: Run a forensic audit on a single transaction.
Unlimited: $299 USD per month for unlimited audits

record.needs_human: The WebFetch summaries paraphrased the docs, and the quotes above come from those summaries, not the raw pages. The fetch of ipayx.ai/docs returned a 404. Check these items: (1) whether API keys work on the free tier or only on paid plans. (2) whether ipx_test_ sandbox keys really exist. (3) the exact scope of the webhooks.
